node.label: Linda Colley
node.date_label: Britons: Forging the Nation (1992) · Captives (2002) · The Ordeal of Elizabeth Marsh: A Woman in World History (2007)
node.description: A historian of Britain, empire and global connections. Her selected works move from the making of British identity to captivity and an individual woman’s transcontinental life. In her 2016 written interview she explains how captivity narratives can expose imperial weakness as well as power, provided they are embedded in other research. She describes Elizabeth Marsh as a way of writing global history through a woman’s constrained and mobile life, reconstructing her through dispersed sources rather than treating biography as an isolated portrait.
